dimensions.label: Decision Delegation
dimensions.descriptor: How far AI participates in moving from options toward a final decision.

dimensions.label: Disclosure
dimensions.descriptor: How willing someone is to share personal thoughts, concerns or experiences with AI.

dimensions.label: Reliance
dimensions.descriptor: How integrated AI has become in completing tasks, thinking or maintaining routine.

dimensions.label: Trust
dimensions.descriptor: How readily AI outputs are treated as credible or usable.

dimensions.label: Verification
dimensions.descriptor: How actively AI outputs are checked, tested or compared with other sources.

dimensions.label: Human Agency
dimensions.descriptor: How clearly personal direction, authorship and responsibility are retained when AI is involved.

dimensions.label: Emotional Regulation
dimensions.descriptor: How much AI participates in processing emotion, stress or internal uncertainty.

dimensions.label: Thought Partnership
dimensions.descriptor: How actively AI is used to develop, challenge or refine ideas.

dimensions.label: Social Transparency
dimensions.descriptor: How openly AI's contribution is acknowledged around other people.

interpretations.copy: AI appears to remain well outside your final decision process. You may use it to gather options or clarify information, but your responses suggest that choosing what happens next stays firmly with you.
AI appears to contribute information without regularly carrying decisions forward. Your responses suggest that it can inform your choices while the final direction is still determined independently.
AI’s role in your decisions appears to vary with the situation. It may help narrow options or organise uncertainty, while the point at which you take over depends on the decision and its importance.

AI appears regularly involved in moving you from options toward a decision. This suggests its contribution extends beyond supplying information and can influence which direction becomes most workable or convincing.
AI appears to play a prominent role in moving decisions toward a conclusion. Your responses suggest that its recommendations can become closely involved in determining what you choose or do next.

You appear to keep clear boundaries around what you share with AI. Its role is likely to remain practical or task-focused, with personal thoughts, concerns and experiences largely kept outside the interaction.

Personal disclosure appears selective and limited. You may share context when it helps complete a task, but your responses suggest that AI is not usually treated as a space for deeper personal openness.

Your openness with AI appears to depend on context. Some interactions may remain practical, while others allow more personal reflection when privacy, convenience or the nature of the issue makes that useful.

You appear comfortable bringing personal thoughts or concerns into some AI conversations. This suggests AI can function as more than a task tool and may provide a private space for reflection or expression.

Personal openness appears to be a prominent part of your AI use. Your responses suggest that AI may be used as a private setting for thoughts, concerns or experiences that are not always expressed elsewhere.
AI appears to remain peripheral to your normal functioning. When it is unavailable, your work and thinking continue without significant disruption.
AI appears useful without being deeply embedded. You may draw on it for selected tasks, but your responses suggest that most of your activity can continue without depending on its availability.

Your reliance on AI appears to shift by task and circumstance. It may be important in some areas while remaining optional in others, producing a relationship that is integrated but not uniformly dependent.
AI appears regularly integrated into how you work or think. Its absence may change the effort, speed or structure of some activities, even when responsibility and direction remain personally held.
AI appears deeply embedded across parts of your routine or thinking. Your responses suggest that its availability can materially affect how easily you begin, organise or complete certain activities.

You appear reluctant to treat AI outputs as credible without substantial independent support. Its answers may be considered, but acceptance is likely to remain separated from presentation quality or apparent confidence.
Your responses suggest a cautious relationship with AI-generated information. You may find outputs useful while still holding back belief or action until the content has earned greater confidence.

Your trust in AI appears conditional. Some outputs may be accepted readily, while unfamiliar, important or uncertain situations prompt more hesitation and a closer evaluation of what the system provides.

You appear regularly willing to treat AI outputs as credible or usable. This suggests that clear and plausible responses can carry meaningful weight in how you understand information or proceed with a task.
Trust appears to be a prominent feature of your AI relationship. Your responses suggest that AI outputs can acquire credibility quickly and may become an influential reference point in your thinking.
Independent checking appears to play a limited role in your AI use. Outputs may often be accepted, adapted or acted on without being compared closely with another source, method or line of reasoning.

Verification appears selective rather than routine. You may check AI when the stakes are visible, while more familiar or convincing outputs are allowed to pass with relatively little additional scrutiny.
Your checking behaviour appears to depend on context. Importance, uncertainty and familiarity may determine whether an AI response is tested carefully or used with lighter review.
You appear regularly inclined to test or compare AI outputs before accepting them. This suggests that receiving an answer and deciding it is reliable remain separate stages in your use.
Active checking appears to be a prominent part of your AI relationship. Your responses suggest that AI is commonly treated as one input to evaluate rather than as a final authority.

Your sense of personal direction appears more easily blurred when AI is involved. The system’s framing, wording or recommendations may become closely intertwined with how you understand authorship and responsibility.

AI appears capable of shaping your direction in ways that are not always clearly separated from your own judgement. Your responses suggest some uncertainty around where the system’s contribution ends and yours begins.
Your sense of agency appears to vary with the interaction. In some situations you retain clear direction, while in others AI’s framing or momentum becomes more involved in shaping the outcome.

You appear to retain a clear sense of direction and responsibility while using AI. Its contribution can influence the process without routinely replacing your authorship of the final judgement or action.

Personal direction appears especially prominent in your AI use. Your responses suggest that AI can contribute extensively while the purpose, judgement and responsibility for what happens next remain clearly yours.
AI appears to have little involvement in how you process emotion, stress or internal uncertainty. Your relationship with it is more likely to remain practical, informational or cognitively focused.
Emotional use appears occasional and bounded. You may sometimes use AI to organise a difficult thought, but it does not appear to be a regular part of how you manage inner experience.
AI’s emotional role appears to depend on the situation. It may help create distance, language or structure around some experiences while remaining absent from others.

AI appears regularly involved in helping you process stress, emotion or internal uncertainty. This suggests the interaction can provide a private structure for reflection as well as practical assistance.

Emotional processing appears to be a prominent part of your AI relationship. Your responses suggest that AI may serve as a recurring private support layer when thoughts or feelings need to be organised.

AI appears to play little part in developing or testing your ideas. Your use is more likely to remain task-specific, with reasoning and creative direction occurring mainly before or outside the interaction.
You appear to use AI more for outputs than for extended thinking. It may help complete or clarify tasks without becoming a regular partner in how ideas are formed or challenged.
AI’s role in your thinking appears to vary by task. It may help expand or refine ideas in some situations while other reasoning remains primarily internal or independently directed.
You appear regularly to use AI to develop, examine or refine ideas. The interaction functions as part of the thinking process rather than only as a way to retrieve information or produce an output.
Thought partnership appears to be a prominent feature of your AI use. Your responses suggest that dialogue with AI is closely integrated into how ideas begin, evolve and are tested.
You appear to keep AI’s contribution largely private or understated around other people. The role it plays in your work or thinking may be more visible to you than it is to those who see the outcome.
You appear selective about acknowledging AI’s contribution. Its involvement may be disclosed when necessary, while many everyday uses remain private, implicit or presented without much explanation.
Your openness about AI use appears to depend on context. Audience, expectations and the type of contribution may determine when its role is stated clearly and when it remains in the background.
You appear generally comfortable acknowledging how AI contributes to your work or thinking. Its involvement is less likely to be concealed when it materially shapes the process or outcome.
Social openness appears to be a prominent part of your AI relationship. Your responses suggest that you are especially willing to make AI’s role visible and discuss how it contributed.

relationship.copy: The first two dimensions point in a similar direction, making the underlying behaviour a more consistent feature of your relationship with AI.
The first two dimensions pull in different directions, showing that AI involvement is more pronounced in one part of your behaviour than another.
The second dimension qualifies the first, showing that greater AI involvement in one area does not automatically remove scrutiny, authorship or personal control.
These dimensions create a meaningful tension: one draws AI further into the process while the other preserves distance, scrutiny or independent direction.
The combination suggests that your behaviour changes with the task or situation rather than following one fixed approach to AI.
All three revealed dimensions sit within the same behavioural family. This concentration is itself meaningful, showing that one part of your AI relationship dominates the current snapshot.
AI appears across several parts of your behavioural life, although its role is expressed differently in each area.
AI appears involved in developing your thinking while the final direction and responsibility remain more clearly personal.
AI may be integrated into your routine without automatically replacing your sense of authorship or responsibility.
Regular AI use sits alongside an active process of deciding which outputs deserve acceptance.
Willingness to use AI-generated information coexists with a separate habit of testing whether it should be believed.
AI can help carry decisions forward while responsibility for the final outcome remains personally recognised.
Private openness with AI does not necessarily translate into equal openness about that relationship around other people.
Personal openness and emotional use reinforce one another, making private reflection a more visible part of the relationship.
AI’s role in developing ideas is strengthened by a readiness to treat its contributions as credible or useful.
AI’s integration into routine extends into how choices are narrowed and carried toward action.
AI may play a meaningful private role even when that part of the relationship is expressed differently in social settings.
AI-generated information can acquire credibility more readily than it is independently tested, bringing acceptance and checking into an uneven relationship.
Caution toward AI-generated information is reinforced by an active habit of checking, keeping credibility dependent on further evidence.
AI is closely involved in developing ideas, while the boundary between its direction and your own authorship appears less clearly defined.
AI is deeply integrated into activity while personal direction appears less clearly separated from the system’s contribution.

transition.copy: These three dimensions show the broad shape of your profile. The next result reveals where your individual pattern becomes more distinctive.
This snapshot shows how several parts of your AI behaviour interact. One further finding brings the individuality of that pattern into clearer view.
